steps.text: [Benchmark & Pricing Researcher]: Fetch and read the EDB whitepaper in full and capture its numbers
steps.do: Use web_search to find the EDB PostgreSQL vs MongoDB whitepaper and its landing page. Use fetch_url on the PDF or page and read the whole document, not just excerpts. Record the publication date, versions, hardware, workload, and the numeric result tables. Label it vendor-funded (EDB). If the tables are not in the text, say so and note what is missing.
steps.output: list: EDB source URL, date, funder, versions, hardware, workload, numeric results, and anything not captured
steps.done_when: The EDB source has URL, publication date (or 'not found'), versions, and numeric results recorded, or each missing item is listed as a gap.

steps.text: [Benchmark & Pricing Researcher]: Gather benchmarks B: standard suites and managed variants
steps.do: 1) Search for TPC-H/TPC-DS or similar suite results and managed-service benchmarks (Aurora PostgreSQL, AlloyDB, Atlas). 2) Fetch the best 3-4 pages. 3) Record author, funder, date, workload, versions, result and relevance. 4) Label vendor-funded results; list gaps.
steps.output: table: source | URL | date | funded by | workload | versions | result | relevance; list: caveats and gaps
steps.done_when: At least 3 sources are tabled with URL and publication date; vendor-funded ones are labelled; gaps are listed (not found is accepted).

steps.text: [Benchmark & Pricing Researcher]: Gather AWS RDS and Aurora PostgreSQL pricing
steps.do: 1) Fetch the official RDS for PostgreSQL and Aurora pricing pages (max 4 fetches). 2) Capture 8-32 vCPU instance classes, storage per GB-month, IOPS/I-O, backup, Multi-AZ/replica, egress and inter-region transfer for eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 and one US region. 3) Mark anything not rendered as not found with the closest cited figure.
steps.output: table: provider | service | region | tier | unit | USD price | URL | date retrieved; list: gaps
steps.done_when: RDS PostgreSQL and Aurora PostgreSQL each have rows with URL and retrieval date or are marked not found; at least one EU region is covered; gaps are listed.

steps.text: [Benchmark & Pricing Researcher]: Gather GCP Cloud SQL and AlloyDB pricing
steps.do: 1) Fetch the official Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL and AlloyDB pricing pages (max 4 fetches). 2) Capture 8-32 vCPU classes, storage per GB-month, backup, HA/read pool, egress and inter-region transfer for europe-west1 or europe-west4 and one US region. 3) Mark anything not rendered as not found with the closest cited figure.
steps.output: table: provider | service | region | tier | unit | USD price | URL | date retrieved; list: gaps
steps.done_when: Cloud SQL and AlloyDB each have rows with URL and retrieval date or are marked not found; at least one EU region is covered; gaps are listed.

steps.text: [Benchmark & Pricing Researcher]: Gather MongoDB Atlas pricing on AWS and GCP
steps.do: 1) Fetch the official Atlas pricing and cluster-tier pages (max 4 fetches). 2) Capture dedicated cluster tiers (M40-M80 class, 8-32 vCPU), storage per GB, backup, data transfer and sharding/size limits for AWS (eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 and one US region) and GCP (europe-west1 or europe-west4 and one US region). 3) Mark anything not rendered as not found with the closest cited figure.
steps.output: table: provider | service | region | tier | unit | USD price | URL | date retrieved; list: gaps
steps.done_when: Atlas on AWS and on GCP each have rows with URL and retrieval date or are marked not found; at least one EU region each is covered; gaps are listed.

steps.text: [Database Prototype Engineer]: Prototype event and dashboard schemas in both databases
steps.do: 1) Check which engines and Python libraries exist. 2) Write schema.sql (partitioned events with tenant_id, dashboard_daily rollup, indexes, optional RLS) and mongo_schema.js (events, rollups, compound indexes, validators). 3) Write generate_data.py and 6 paired queries (queries.sql, queries_mongo.py). 4) Write schema_notes.md stating engine availability and design notes.
steps.output: code: schema.sql, mongo_schema.js, generate_data.py, queries.sql, queries_mongo.py; list: engine availability and design notes in schema_notes.md
steps.done_when: Both schema files and the generator exist; 6 paired queries exist; schema_notes.md states engine availability.

steps.text: [Database Prototype Engineer]: Test the prototypes with synthetic multi-tenant data
steps.do: 1) Load generated data into available engines or the labelled proxy. 2) Run the 6 queries 3 times each, take medians, and check row counts match across sides. 3) Run the tenant-isolation check. 4) Record stored sizes and write results.csv. 5) List limitations and what a real 10 TB test needs.
steps.output: table: test | PostgreSQL result | MongoDB result | engine or proxy | notes; file results.csv; list: limitations
steps.done_when: results.csv exists with at least 6 query rows plus an isolation row; each row is labelled real-engine or proxy; a limitations list is given.

steps.text: [Cloud Cost Analyst]: Estimate monthly cost for 50 tenants x 200 GB at 5,000 queries/min
steps.do: 1) Size instances and storage from 10 TB raw, 83.3 qps peak and the footprint assumptions. 2) Build cost_model.xlsx (Assumptions, Prices, Model, Summary) with formulas. 3) Cover RDS, Aurora, Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Atlas-AWS and Atlas-GCP in low/base/high scenarios plus EU share 20/50/100%. 4) Re-check totals with calc. 5) Give per-tenant cost and main cost drivers.
steps.output: table: provider | database | scenario | monthly USD | USD per tenant; file cost_model.xlsx
steps.done_when: cost_model.xlsx has formulas and a Summary sheet; each of the 6 combinations has 3 scenarios; totals match a calc re-computation; figures are labelled estimates.

steps.text: [Compliance & Delivery Lead]: GDPR framework: Chapter V transfers, SCCs, DPF, DPAs, erasure
steps.do: 1) Fetch at most 4 official sources (EDPB, European Commission, EUR-Lex, provider DPA pages). 2) Summarise Chapter V transfer mechanisms, SCCs, EU-US DPF status and transfer impact assessments. 3) Summarise DPA/sub-processor duties and erasure/DSR obligations. 4) Cite URL and access date for each claim and add a not-legal-advice statement.
steps.output: memo: GDPR legal framework with cited official sources and access dates
steps.done_when: The framework covers transfers, SCCs, DPF status, DPAs and erasure; each claim cites an official URL with an access date; a not-legal-advice statement is included.

steps.text: [Compliance & Delivery Lead]: GDPR residency on AWS and GCP: RDS, Aurora, Cloud SQL, AlloyDB
steps.do: 1) Fetch up to 4 AWS and GCP documentation pages on EU regions, backups, replicas, support access and telemetry. 2) For RDS, Aurora, Cloud SQL and AlloyDB, assess EU-region hosting and where backups, replicas, snapshots, logs and support access can leave the EU. 3) Note how erasure works in PostgreSQL. 4) Cite URL and access date for each claim.
steps.output: table: service | EU regions | backups/replicas | support access and telemetry | erasure | URL and date; list: gaps
steps.done_when: The table has one row each for RDS, Aurora, Cloud SQL and AlloyDB; each row covers hosting, backups, support access and erasure; every claim has an official URL and access date.

steps.text: [Compliance & Delivery Lead]: GDPR residency on Atlas, per-provider comparison and counsel checklist
steps.do: 1) Fetch up to 3 Atlas documentation pages on region pinning, global clusters, backup region, support access and erasure. 2) Assess Atlas on AWS and on GCP. 3) State the shared-database implication: EU tenants need separate EU and non-EU clusters. 4) Write a comparison table across all 6 combinations using step 10, a counsel checklist and a not-legal-advice statement.
steps.output: memo: GDPR residency assessment with 6-row comparison table and counsel checklist
steps.done_when: Atlas hosting, backup, support access and erasure are assessed with official URLs and dates; the 6-row comparison table is present; the counsel checklist and a not-legal-advice statement are included.

steps.text: [Compliance & Delivery Lead]: Draft memo core: recommendation, evidence, cost table, GDPR
steps.do: 1) Start memo_part1.md with the required opening line. 2) Weigh benchmark, cost, GDPR and prototype evidence and choose one database and one primary provider with confidence and flip conditions. 3) Summarise evidence: benchmarks with bias caveats, the cost table from step 8, prototype findings with proxy limits. 4) Add the GDPR section from steps 9-11. 5) Save memo_part1.md.
steps.output: memo: memo core with recommendation, evidence, cost table and GDPR section; file memo_part1.md
steps.done_when: memo_part1.md exists and opens with the required line; it names one database and provider with confidence and flip conditions; it contains the cost table and GDPR section; proxy results are not used as performance evidence.

steps.text: [Compliance & Delivery Lead]: Add risk table and 90-day migration plan; save memo_draft.docx
steps.do: 1) Read memo_part1.md. 2) Write a risk table of at least 8 rows (risk | likelihood | impact | mitigation | owner). 3) Write the 90-day plan in three 30-day phases with week-level milestones, owners by role from a 12-person team and go/no-go gates at days 30, 60, 90; schedule a real-engine test in the first 30 days if step 7 was proxy. 4) Combine into memo_draft.docx with the docx skill (fallback python-docx, then memo_draft.md).
steps.output: memo: full memo draft with risk table and 90-day plan; file memo_draft.docx
steps.done_when: memo_draft.docx exists and still opens with the required line; the risk table has 8+ rows with owners; the 90-day plan has week-level milestones; gates are set at days 30, 60, 90.

steps.text: [Benchmark & Pricing Researcher]: Verify pricing and benchmark URLs cited in the memo
steps.do: 1) Pick 4 URLs cited in the memo (at least 2 pricing, at least 1 benchmark). 2) Re-fetch each and compare the quoted figure, date and bias label. 3) Check the memo states vendor-funded bias where applicable. 4) Give a verdict with confirmed items, discrepancies and unverifiable items.
steps.output: list: verdict (pass / pass with corrections / fail), confirmed items, discrepancies with corrections, unverifiable items
steps.done_when: 4 URLs are re-fetched and compared; vendor-bias statements are checked; a verdict is stated.

steps.text: [Benchmark & Pricing Researcher]: Verify GDPR sources cited in the memo
steps.do: 1) Pick 3-4 official GDPR/provider URLs cited in the memo and re-fetch them. 2) Compare each memo claim (DPF status, SCCs, region/backup/support-access statements) to the page. 3) Check the not-legal-advice statement and counsel checklist exist. 4) Give a verdict with confirmed items, discrepancies and unverifiable items.
steps.output: list: verdict (pass / pass with corrections / fail), confirmed items, discrepancies with corrections, unverifiable items
steps.done_when: At least 3 GDPR/provider URLs are re-fetched and compared to the memo; a verdict is stated.

steps.text: [Database Prototype Engineer]: Verify cost model totals by independent recomputation
steps.do: 1) Read cost_model.xlsx input cells and formulas. 2) Recompute at least 5 Summary totals (across different providers and scenarios) with calc. 3) Check the memo's cost table matches the Summary. 4) Give a verdict with discrepancies.
steps.output: list: verdict (pass / pass with corrections / fail), totals recomputed, discrepancies with corrections, unverifiable items
steps.done_when: At least 5 totals are recomputed with calc and compared to the workbook and the memo; a verdict is stated.

steps.text: [Cloud Cost Analyst]: Verify memo claims against prototype files and plan consistency
steps.do: 1) Read results.csv, schema_notes.md and the schema files; check each memo claim about the prototype and tests against them and that proxy results are not used as performance evidence. 2) Check the recommendation follows from the evidence. 3) Check the risk table and 90-day plan are consistent (owners, dates, gates). 4) Give a verdict with corrections.
steps.output: list: verdict (pass / pass with corrections / fail), confirmed claims, mismatches with corrections, consistency issues
steps.done_when: Every memo claim about prototype and test results is checked against the files; plan and risk-table consistency is checked; a verdict is stated.

steps.text: [Memo Assembler]: Assemble the final recommendation memo
steps.do: 1) Start with the required opening line. 2) Merge the memo draft with the cost table, GDPR assessment, benchmark evidence and test results into eight sections: Recommendation, Evidence, Monthly cost table, GDPR assessment, Prototype results, Risk table, 90-day plan, Limitations. 3) Apply all verifier corrections or list unresolved ones under Limitations. 4) Keep citations and dates.
steps.output: memo: final recommendation memo with cost table, risk table, 90-day plan and limitations
steps.done_when: The memo opens with the required line; all eight sections are present; every verifier correction is applied or listed under Limitations.

steps.text: [Benchmark & Pricing Researcher]: Find and read 2-3 independent or newer benchmarks
steps.do: Use web_search for OnGres, academic papers and YCSB-based PostgreSQL vs MongoDB comparisons, and for results newer than 2019. Use fetch_url on the best 2-3 pages and read each one in full. Record author, funder, exact date, workload, versions, result and relevance to a shared-database multi-tenant dashboard workload. Label vendor-funded ones. Stop after 3 fetches and list what was not found.
steps.output: list: for each source, URL, date, funder, workload, versions, result, relevance, plus gaps
steps.done_when: At least 2 further sources are recorded with URL and date, vendor-funded ones are labelled, and gaps are listed (not found is accepted).

steps.text: [Benchmark & Pricing Researcher]: Merge both sub-step results into the final table, caveats and gaps list
steps.do: Combine the earlier sub-step results into one table with a row per source and no new research. Quote only figures that were recorded with a source and a date. Label vendor-funded results and write the caveats and gaps list, including the tech-insider.org article's exact date if it was found.
steps.output: table: source | URL | date | funded by | workload | versions | result | relevance; list: caveats and gaps
steps.done_when: At least 3 sources are tabled with URL and publication date; vendor-funded ones are labelled; gaps are listed (not found is accepted).
